stories.title: Google Issues Chrome Security Update for Eighth Actively Exploited Zero-Day of 2026
stories.summary: Google on Monday released updates to patch nine security vulnerabilities, including one that has come under active exploitation in the wild. The high-severity vulnerability, assigned the CVE identifier CVE-2026-125350 (CVSS score: N/A), has been described as a use-after-free bug in the XML component. stories.title: SEGA newsletter data breach exposes 2.2 million email addresses
stories.summary: Japanese gaming giant SEGA has disclosed that a data breach at its third-party newsletter provider, ARARA, exposed the email addresses of 2.2 million newsletter subscribers.

stories.title: Binance denies data breach after alleged ShinyHunters claims
stories.summary: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has denied claims of a new security breach made by a threat actor using the 'ShinyHunters' handle on a newly emerged underground cybercrime forum.

stories.title: Google patches eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks this year
stories.summary: Google has released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks, the eighth such flaw since the start of the year.

stories.title: N-able Takes N-central Offline as Researcher Drops Over 30 Zero-Days
stories.summary: Attackers could exploit the flaws for remote code execution, credential theft, and administrator account creation.

stories.title: Revolve Puts Data Breach Victim Count at 1.5 Million
stories.summary: Online fashion retailer Revolve has told regulators that the September cyberattack affected more than 1.5 million individuals.

stories.title: Bitter Hackers Deploy New PapRAT Backdoor in Cyberespionage Campaign Targeting South Asia
stories.summary: The South Asian cyber espionage group known as Bitter (aka APT-C-08, APT-Q-37, Hazy Tiger, Orange Yali, T-APT-17, and TA397) has been observed targeting South Asian organizations with a previously unreported remote access trojan called PapRAT. stories.title: Turla hackers use new Cereal malware to spy on govt Exchange servers
stories.summary: The Russian state-backed threat group Turla has been using a new malicious toolset called 'Cereal' to intercept emails on Microsoft Exchange servers at government organizations.
